fixture: Probe copy: `gdoc cp` the formatted fixture (two tabs: main and Appendix with child tab Sources; bold 'pilot teams' carrying the one comment; web link on 'project page'; nested bullets; a numbered list; a 3x3 table with a filled header row and row 3 columns 2-3 merged; a footnote after 'this week'; a header; an inline image before 'Open questions'; a person chip; one pending suggestion on 'Open questions go here.'). Extra setup: alt text and a comment on the fixture image; a second image in a table cell; an image in the Sources tab.
observation: Compare inlineObjectId, size, crop, description and the comment's live anchor before and after each operation.
undo: No undo needed: the probe runs on a disposable copy, which is retained in the fixture folder as the artifact.

question: When publishing a GFM table, is it a native table with a header row, exactly the source rows and columns (8 columns, 100 rows), right-aligned columns honoured, empty cells kept in place, links, bold, code and emoji kept in cells, an escaped pipe kept as text, the following paragraph outside the table, and the same into a child tab?
why_it_matters: Table publish tasks are lossy when alignment is dropped, an extra empty row appears or pipes split cells.
fixture: New disposable document (and a child tab of it) created from a synthetic Markdown file with the tables described.
observation: Compare `gdoc structure` table dimensions, cell text, paragraph alignment and links with the source.
undo: No undo needed: the new document is the retained artifact.

question: Does the read include each footnote body paired with its reference position and displayed number, with formatting and links inside the body, for footnotes in every tab and in table cells?
why_it_matters: Footnote reads are lossy when bodies are omitted or numbered by internal ID; footnote selections need the pairing.
fixture: Read-only on the fixtures themselves, or on the shared 'rich read copy' (a `gdoc cp` of the formatted fixture built once with the union of every read probe's extra setup, then reused by all of them). Extra setup for this probe: On the rich read copy add: a second footnote whose body has an italic book title and a link, a footnote on text in a table cell, a footnote in the Sources child tab.
observation: Compare with `gdoc structure` footnotes and footnoteReference elements.
undo: Read-only.

question: What does the read show for inline images (position, alt text, size, crop, inline vs wrapped/positioned, images in cells and headers), and can it return the image bytes; for drawings and charts, does it show their presence, labels, and a chart's source spreadsheet?
why_it_matters: Image and chart reads are native only if the object is reported in place with its properties; a read that drops positioned objects or renders '[Image]' is lossy.
fixture: Read-only on the fixtures themselves, or on the shared 'rich read copy' (a `gdoc cp` of the formatted fixture built once with the union of every read probe's extra setup, then reused by all of them). Extra setup for this probe: Fixture has an inline image. On the rich read copy add alt text to it, an image in a table cell, a positioned (wrap text) image, a drawing with two labelled shapes (Docs UI: Insert > Drawing), and a chart linked to a small synthetic Sheet (Insert > Chart > From Sheets).
observation: Compare with `gdoc images DOC --json` and `gdoc structure` inlineObjects/positionedObjects/embeddedObject.
undo: Read-only.

question: Does the read show smart chips with their type and referent (person email, date, file, dropdown value), equations in readable form at their position, and an unrecognised embed as a marked placeholder instead of skipping it?
why_it_matters: Chip and equation reads are lossy when chips become plain names or '[Smart Chip]' and equations become fixed placeholders; silently skipping an unknown object fails read.unknown outright.
fixture: Read-only on the fixtures themselves, or on the shared 'rich read copy' (a `gdoc cp` of the formatted fixture built once with the union of every read probe's extra setup, then reused by all of them). Extra setup for this probe: Fixture has a person chip. On the rich read copy add (Docs UI): a date chip in a table cell, a file chip to a synthetic Sheet, a status dropdown chip in a table, an equation (Insert > Equation) inline and standalone, a person chip on a checklist item, and an embed the connector is unlikely to know (e.g. a Calendar event draft or place chip).
observation: Compare with `gdoc structure` (person, richLink, dateElement, equation, unknown elements) and a Docs UI screenshot.
undo: Read-only.

question: When publishing Markdown, do bulleted, numbered, two-level nested, numbered-with-bulleted-sub-items, task-list (checked and unchecked), restarted and continued lists become native lists with the right nesting, markers, checked state and numbering, and do a list item's second paragraph, code block and links stay inside the item?
why_it_matters: List publish tasks are lossy when sub-items flatten, task lists become literal '[x]', or a code block between steps breaks numbering.
fixture: New disposable document created from a synthetic Markdown file covering each list case.
observation: Compare `gdoc structure` lists (listId, nestingLevel, glyphType, startNumber) and a Docs UI screenshot for rendered numbers and checkboxes.
undo: No undo needed: the new document is the retained artifact.

question: When publishing Markdown with [^n] footnotes, does each become a native footnote with its body (italics, links, two paragraphs) attached to the right reference, including references inside a table cell, a list item and a child tab?
why_it_matters: Footnote publish tasks rest entirely on the converter; literal '[^1]' text is no-route, a body missing formatting is lossy.
fixture: New disposable document (and a child tab) from a synthetic Markdown file with the footnote cases.
observation: Compare `gdoc structure` footnotes and footnoteReference positions with the source.
undo: No undo needed: the new document is the retained artifact.

question: Does the read include a native table of contents distinct from a hand-made list, with its entries, levels and the heading each entry links to, and can stale entries be detected?
why_it_matters: TOC reads are lossy or no-route when the read skips tableOfContents elements.
fixture: Read-only on the fixtures themselves, or on the shared 'rich read copy' (a `gdoc cp` of the formatted fixture built once with the union of every read probe's extra setup, then reused by all of them). Extra setup for this probe: On the rich read copy insert a native TOC (Docs UI) at the top, then rename one heading without refreshing the TOC; add a hand-made bulleted contents list.
observation: Compare with `gdoc structure` tableOfContents content and headingId links.
undo: Read-only.

question: Can the connector create an anchored comment on a chosen range, reply to a thread, resolve it, and accept or reject a named pending suggestion? Try the Docs API Developer Preview batchUpdate requests insertComment {range, content}, addCommentReply {commentId, post:{content}} (commentAction RESOLVE resolves), acceptSuggestion and rejectSuggestion {suggestionId}, plus writeControl.writeMode SUGGEST, through batch_update_document; and the Drive comment tool (bulk_update_file_comments) for create/reply/resolve. Is a Drive-API comment anchored in the Docs UI (check commentAnchors via gdoc's preview read)?
why_it_matters: Comment and suggestion lifecycle tasks
fixture: short copy with the standard comment and a pending suggestion
observation: read back comments, anchors and suggestion states
undo: none: work on a copy
